clue.text: Standard features with military badge

definitions.note: a standard is a flag, here the US flag

parts.note: a film that features an actor stars them, so 'features' is the verb stars
and means together with
stripes are the chevrons on a sleeve showing military rank

explanation.surface: A description of some standard kit: certain features plus a soldier's badge of rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like an adjective meaning ordinary, but it is a flag, and 'features' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stars and Stripes is the national flag of the United States, and a standard is a flag.

clue.text: Crossword writer's work background

definitions.meaning: a crossword compiler is called a setter
the surroundings or backdrop of a scene or story

explanation.definitionFit: Compilers set puzzles, so their job is setting; a story's setting is its backdrop.

clue.text: Jelly, equally still

parts.note: as in 'as tall as' expresses equality
a still is a photograph, a pic for short

explanation.surface: A wobbly jelly described as being just as motionless as something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like an adverb or adjective but is a noun: a still photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Bond following hit comedy

indicators.note: places the word for bond after the word for hit in the answer

parts.note: a slap is a hit with the open hand
to bond is to stick together

explanation.surface: A James Bond-style sequel to a box-office hit, played for laughs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests the spy, but it is the verb meaning adhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is boisterous physical comedy, named after a clown's prop bat.

clue.text: OK taking touch before heavy weight lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the letters are read upwards, i.e. backwards
puts the word for touch ahead of the weight before the whole is turned

parts.note: a dab is a light touch
a ton is a large unit of weight

explanation.surface: A weightlifter, given a quick touch first, manages a heavy lift — not a bad effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' reverses DABTON as a whole, giving NOT BAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is not bad is a mild approval, meaning it is acceptable or fine.

clue.text: Therefore, one in airport has found way out

parts.note: so means therefore

indicators.note: puts the one inside the airport name

parts.note: Luton is an airport north of London
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone lost at an airport finally locates the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: LUTON is an airport serving London.
explanation.definitionFit: A solution is a way out of a problem or difficulty.

clue.text: Collar uneven, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: says the word for uneven is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a rough surface is uneven

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a collar is lopsided, judging by how it sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruff is a stiff frilled collar of Elizabethan fashion.

clue.text: Very rare comic

definitions.meaning: so rare that no price can be put on it

explanation.definitionFit: Priceless means invaluable, and colloquially describes something extremely funny.

clue.text: Drunk has arrived — ha!

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
someone who has arrived is here

explanation.surface: A drunk turns up and someone laughs triumphantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' is a noun, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: So there! is a triumphant exclamation, like a taunting ha!

clue.text: Salute, installing leader of government in nautical post

indicators.note: the toast takes in the leader inside it

parts.note: to toast someone is to salute them with a drink
PM is short for Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A ceremony greets a new head of government at a naval post.
explanation.definitionFit: A topmast is the section of a ship's mast above the lower mast.

clue.text: Red mullet's tail by itself, cooked

indicators.note: by means next to, so the tail letter sits beside the reworked word
cooked means the letters are worked over into a new order
the tail of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A red mullet's tail is cooked on its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges ITSELF to LEFTIS, with T (mullet's tail) beside it. 'Red mullet' is a fish, but 'Red' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is a common name for a left-wing socialist or communist, a leftist.

clue.text: Endless cricket initially boring as tennis, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly means the letters end up in an unexpected order
takes only the opening letter of the word cricket

explanation.surface: Someone complains that cricket is as boring as tennis and goes on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges C, AS and TENNIS; 'boring' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incessant never stops, going on without end.

clue.text: Listening to children, give up

indicators.note: says the word for children is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: seed means offspring, children

explanation.surface: A parent, after hearing the kids out, surrenders.
explanation.walkthrough: Seed for offspring is biblical usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender or hand over, such as territory.

clue.text: Rounding first of defenders, briefly follow winger

indicators.note: the phrase for follow goes around the letter taken
briefly means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: to go with is to follow or accompany

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of defenders

explanation.surface: A football winger dribbles round a defender and the others chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' shortens GO WITH to GO WIT. 'winger' suggests football; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A godwit is a long-billed wading bird, and anything with wings can be called a winger in crosswords.

clue.text: Minister plugging domestic work record

indicators.note: the minister fills a gap inside the domestic work

parts.note: DIY is do-it-yourself home improvement
a rector is a parish minister

explanation.surface: A clergyman fixing things around the house sets a record.
explanation.definitionFit: A directory is a listing such as names and addresses, a kind of reference record.

clue.text: Certain island behind fraud

indicators.note: puts the island after the fraud

parts.note: a con is a swindle
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Someone is sure that an island is behind a scam.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete as in concrete evidence means definite or certain.

clue.text: Lower a rail so diverted underneath church

indicators.note: in a down clue the rearranged letters sit below the church
diverted means the letters are sent off in another order

explanation.surface: A railway line is lowered and rerouted beneath a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is not 'more low' but 'one that lows', a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Charolais is a breed of beef cattle, and cattle low, so a cow is a lower.

clue.text: Natural reaction isn't unusual in case of cat

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are in an uncommon arrangement
the case of a word is its outside letters

explanation.surface: A cat's natural reaction isn't unusual in this situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges ISNT to INST; 'case of cat' gives CT.
explanation.definitionFit: An instinct is an innate, unlearned response, a reaction that comes naturally.

clue.text: Noticeable beating

explanation.definitionFit: Striking describes something eye-catching, and also the act of hitting.

clue.text: Fruit pots from China

definitions.meaning: ... ware is a type of glazed Japanese earthenware

explanation.surface: Fruit served in pots imported from China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' at the start of a phrase looks like the country, but it means crockery: Satsuma ware comes from Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Satsuma names both a mandarin-type orange and a kind of Japanese pottery.

clue.text: Pester hearty on tour of ship

indicators.note: going on a tour of something means going all round it

parts.note: hale means healthy, hearty
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A cheery passenger badgers people while touring a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To hassle someone is to harass or keep bothering them.

clue.text: Rank deal: more cut off

indicators.note: off means the letters are disordered
cut means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A dodgy bargain: no more deals are offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks MORE to MOR; 'off' rearranges DEAL with MOR. 'Rank' looks like an adjective (foul) but is a title.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the rank or title of an earl, a degree of nobility.

clue.text: Don: boy biting cheek

indicators.note: the boy closes around the cheek as if in his teeth

parts.note: a son is a boy
lip means impudence, cheek

explanation.surface: An academic is cheeked by a boy who bites back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' suggests a university lecturer; here it is the verb meaning put on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip on a garment is to put it on quickly, which is what donning means.

clue.text: Minute arachnid

definitions.meaning: a ... is a moment, as in 'just a ...'
a blood-sucking parasite related to spiders

explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like an adjective, 'tiny'; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: In British speech a tick is a brief moment; the parasite is a mite-like arachnid.

clue.text: Brothers over six feet? Too much to ask

parts.note: a person over six feet is tall; the query flags the playful reading
a religious order is a body of brothers

explanation.surface: A wry aside that a fraternity of giants would be a big request.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is an unreasonably demanding task or request.

clue.text: The same ludicrous papers sent over

indicators.note: sent over means flipped, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: OTT is over the top, i.e. absurdly excessive
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: The same ridiculous documents were dispatched again.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same again, used to avoid repeating what was just said.

clue.text: Material on floor in prison I levered up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
the answer lies inside the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A prisoner prises up the floor covering of the cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'levered' is part of the run of letters, not a separate instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Lino, short for linoleum, is a sheet floor covering.

clue.text: Perfect, best boy behind you, finally

indicators.note: puts best boy after the letter from you
takes only the last letter of you

parts.note: top means best
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A best boy, the film crew role, standing behind you at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best boy' reads as the film-crew title, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian describes an idealised, flawless state, as in More's Utopia.

clue.text: Firmly established capitals of Togo, Eritrea and Djibouti found on map

indicators.note: the capitals come next to the map, placed after it

parts.note: a plan is a map or diagram

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the three country names

explanation.surface: Three African countries' capitals are located on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitals' suggests cities like Lomé; here it means capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something planted is set firmly in place, like a seedling in the ground.

clue.text: Party nominators toyed with desperate choice

indicators.note: playing with the letters puts them in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Party selectors play around with a candidate chosen in desperation.
explanation.definitionFit: Any port in a storm is the proverb for accepting any option when in trouble.
